title: One Seputeh: a boutique tower beside Thean Hou Temple.
videoTitle: PROPERTY REVIEW #462 | ONE SEPUTEH, KUALA LUMPUR
excerpt: A new single-tower launch of 383 units off Jalan Syed Putra, a short drive from KL Sentral and Mid Valley. Sean looks at its dual-key layouts, its rooftop and its unusual neighbours.
takeaways: 383 freehold units in one tower, 10 a floor with six lifts, and a level-50 sky deck facing the KL skyline.
About RM950 to RM1,000 psf; a dual-key two-bedroom costs about RM600,000 to RM700,000-plus.
A narrow road, a cemetery next door, a shared retail entrance and a developer new to the Klang Valley are the concerns.

sections.heading: What sets it apart
paragraphs: One Seputeh is a single freehold tower of 383 units: shops and a hotel-style lobby at ground level, an elevated car park, a level-9 resort deck with a 30 m saltwater infinity pool, quiet rooms and a lawn, and a sky deck at level 50 with a gym, hall and lounge. Ten units share each floor and six lifts, and the corridors have no voids, so every room looks outward.

Many layouts are dual-key. Sean tours a two-bedroom, two-bathroom dual-key unit: a studio with its own bathroom and pantry and a one-bedroom unit, sharing a foyer, with 3.3 m ceilings and full-height windows. The project sells at about RM950 to RM1,000 psf, so this unit costs about RM600,000 to RM700,000-plus.

sections.heading: Where it is
paragraphs: It is off Jalan Syed Putra, beside Thean Hou Temple and SJK(C) Kuen Cheng 2, with KL Sentral across the highway and Mid Valley and KL Eco City about 10 minutes' drive away. Seputeh is an old, low-rise neighbourhood of bungalows and townhouses, with no rail station on this side of the highway. A Chinese cemetery adjoins the site, and the temple draws heavy crowds at festivals.

pros: Seputeh's balance of city and nature: KL Sentral, Bangsar, Mid Valley and KL Eco City are close, yet the neighbourhood stays low-rise and green. Sean likes that it isn't on a rail line, which keeps it private; anyone who relies on public transport should look across the highway.
Low density: 383 units in one tower, with 10 a floor sharing six lifts, is almost impossible to find in the city at this budget.

No shortcuts on design: a hotel-like lobby, voidless corridors, a quiet zone between the lawn and a 30 m saltwater infinity pool, and the level-50 rooftop. The dual-key layouts suit working couples without children or families with parents moving in, and Sean expects rents to cover the instalment easily, though he would have liked slightly bigger units.
cons: The micro site: old apartments and offices next door, and a narrow road that jams after school, which the developer has committed to widening to three lanes. A cemetery adjoins the site; the lift core and wing walls keep it out of view from every unit but one, though the rooftop overlooks it.
A shared ground floor: five shop lots share the entrance with residents, so a busy retail strip costs privacy and an empty one helps no one. The developer will hold and manage the shops.

The developer: a private firm with 28 years in property, better known for solar, building its first Klang Valley project. Its role as white knight reviving a stalled project in Taiping shows its finances, so Sean isn't worried, and a boutique developer can price more keenly than a listed one.

closing: Refreshing dual-key layouts at an attractive price for Seputeh, best for city workers who value privacy over a train station.
sourceNote: Based on Sean's full English captions for this August 2026 episode and its video description. The 3 on 3 follows the three things he likes and the three he doesn't, in his order, at the end of the video. Sean visited at the invitation of a friend at the developer, whose revived project in Taiping he also covered; prices are those he quoted at launch.
